items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-12-09
items.q: he was a half cousin to my mother in any family.

ctx.x: But anyway, now, would you agree that there were different, that there were different styles of playing, but then that it wasn't necessary in different areas of the city?

No, I don't, like the styles, maybe I didn't pay attention. But I don't think they were in different styles. I do think they, they were, the Creole musicians, those times, they, uh, everybody went, from Georgia, went to, uh, Old Man Teal, you know, for the lessons they learned to read. Uh, there was another old man, was a Chalini, he was a male, he brought out, all the men he brought out, they were good readers, but they never could, they, they'd no place except in one. And I knew of, anywhere, was, uh, uh, Joe…
